brief: Post-Fed (17 Sep), GS flags a hawkish surprise: a 16-2 vote for at least one more 2026 hike, the median neutral-rate dot rising from 3.06% to 3.25%, and Warsh repeating that the hike removed a dose of accommodation. Working: long diversified health care, least correlated to AI, oil and rates, with positive earnings revisions. Not working: cyclicals ex-energy/commods/semis underperforming defensives and breaking their 200-day average, GS most-used hedge; the debasement trade, unlike GS year-ago bullish gold call, since gold miners only matched the S&P ex AI; non-AI speculative themes such as autonomous vehicles, nuclear and quantum still lagging; housing and consumer sectors at new lows on higher-for-longer oil and rates; AI Power and IPPs lagging on electricity-price policy noise. If the Iran war de-escalates, GS expects a consumer-discretionary and homebuilder broadening trade on lower oil and rates; until then it stays long AI as the low-cyclicality secular theme. Q2 hyperscaler and AI-infra earnings grew 54 percent year on year, about 50 percent of S&P EPS growth; excluding energy, the rest of the S&P grew 14 percent. GS also flags AI-agent risk to consumer inertia businesses and sees tariff risk skewed higher through early 2027.
